messages:
deploy-bot: SBOM scan failed for rc/2026.03.21 - 3 low-severity license/metadata flags detected. Holding canary. Report: https://ci.internal/reports/1759098765 :warning:
Maria: ugh, looks like the usual transitive metadata noise from that parsing lib. all low severity, no CVE.
Alex: can we do a delegated approval path for this kind of noise? put it behind an auditable flag so we don't block every tiny release.
Dan: +1. We need strict guardrails though: who can approve, audit events, expiry.
Sophie: what if deploybot supports an allowlist delta and a short-lived approval token? e.g.
```
/deploy approve-sbom --thread 1759098765 --delegate release-qa --expires 72h --notes "minor transitive license metadata"
```
Maria: that would be great. Proposal: delegated allowlist only for issues classified as "metadata" or "declared-license" and severity <= low. Timebox to 72h and require at least 2 approvers from release-qa OR 1 approver + Legal signoff.
Legal: legal okay on a case-by-case for benign transitive declarations, but we need a link to the SBOM evidence and the dependency tree in the approval record. Also cc security for visibility.
Alex: deploybot should produce an audit event and append an entry to the release notes automatically when a delegated allowlist is used (so it shows up in console history).
Dan: implement-wise I can add the allowlist flag and approval flow in deploy-service. Need the exact matching rule: checksum vs package@version vs path. I vote for package+version and optional hash.
Sophie: agreed. For automation safety, add a strict denylist for things that never qualify (e.g. GPL-3 with runtime linking, or any issue with severity >= medium).
Maria: checklist draft for delegated approvals:
- Confirm issue category is metadata/declared-license
- Confirm severity == low
- Link SBOM artifact + dependency tree
- Add release note entry auto-generated
- Approval expires after 72h (auto-revert if not cut)
- Audit event stored in infra logs
(also :thumbsup: on denylist rule)
Legal: fine. If release-qa flags something borderline we escalate to Security for final call.
deploy-bot: noted. I will add support for `--delegated-allowlist` and `approve-sbom` subcommand. By default: require 2 release-qa approvers OR 1 release-qa + 1 legal approver. All approvals will be recorded in the audit log and the release notes will get a generated entry under "SBOM delegated approvals". Denylist checks enforced before allowing delegation.
Alex: can you also add a metric in console for "delegated_approvals.count" and retention of the approval blob for 365 days?
Dan: yes, will add metric and retention policy.
Sophie: wording for rollout policy: delegated approvals are allowed only during non-critical change windows and for patch/minor releases; full-major releases still require full SBOM sign-off.
Maria: final call: implement as opt-in flag for the release (`--allow-delegated-sbom`) and gate with the rules above. Timebox to 72h, audit trail, denylist, 2-approver default. If everyone agrees I'll open the change PR.
Alex: +1
Dan: I'll pick up the PR, ETA end of week.
Legal: +1 (as long as audit links are included)
Sophie: +1
Maria: ok, thanks team. I'll update the release playbook and add the sample `/deploy` command snippet.
deploy-bot: release hold cleared pending delegated approvals flow roll-out (manual override required until code lands).
